name: OpenConditions Ingest
description: Fetches open road-condition, fuel-price, parking and EV-charging feeds (NDW, Autobahn, Digitraffic, DriveBC, WZDx, Tankerkoenig, ParkAPI, BNetzA, OCPI and DATEX II charging publishers, and others), normalises them to the canonical model, and writes them to the shared PostGIS `conditions` schema for OpenMapX to read. Also serves public, rate-limited emitter feeds (GeoJSON, TraFF, DATEX II, GTFS-RT, JSON-LD, Valhalla exclusions, SSE).
author: OpenConditions

DATABASE_URL.title: Database URL
DATABASE_URL.description: Required. PostgreSQL/PostGIS connection URL of the shared OpenMapX database, e.g. postgresql://postgres:<POSTGRES_PASSWORD>@postgis:5432/openmapx. The service refuses to start without it.

OPENCONDITIONS_OPERATOR_TOKEN.title: Operator token
OPENCONDITIONS_OPERATOR_TOKEN.description: Bearer token granting the operator scope (restricted sources, no rate limit); at least 32 characters, or the service fails boot. Must equal OpenMapX's own OPENCONDITIONS_OPERATOR_TOKEN, which app-api and the data-manager send. Unset, OpenMapX reads in the public scope and serves none of the restricted sources, those whose licence or terms keep their records from public redistribution: Tankerkönig (DE), E-Control (AT) and OpenStreetMap fuel stations, OpenStreetMap, BNLS (FR) and Mobidrom Park+Ride (DE) car parks, and OpenStreetMap, Open Charge Map and NAP Slovenija charge points.

SEGMENT_REGIONS.title: Road graph regions
SEGMENT_REGIONS.description: Complete JSON array of {id,bbox,tz,pbfUrls?,highwayClasses?}. Used by import, binding coverage and speed profiles. Unset or [] means no configured graph coverage. See graph-binding documentation.

SEGMENT_HIGHWAY_CLASSES.title: Road graph highway classes
SEGMENT_HIGHWAY_CLASSES.description: Comma-separated OSM highway values the road-graph import keeps. Empty: the built-in set.

BIND_ENABLED.title: Bind records to the road graph
BIND_ENABLED.description: "false" turns binding records to road-graph segments off. Empty: on.

BIND_MAX_OFFSET_M.title: Binding max offset (m)
BIND_MAX_OFFSET_M.description: How far a record's geometry may lie from a segment and still bind to it. Empty: the built-in default.

BIND_CONCURRENCY.title: Binding concurrency
BIND_CONCURRENCY.description: Records bound in parallel. Empty: the built-in default.

OPENLR_RESOLVER_URL.title: OpenLR resolver URL
OPENLR_RESOLVER_URL.description: URL of the OpenLR map-match resolver service. Empty: observations that carry only OpenLR (no coordinates) are dropped rather than resolved.

OPENCONDITIONS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS.title: Feed fetch timeout (ms)
OPENCONDITIONS_FETCH_TIMEOUT_MS.description: Timeout of every feed fetch. Empty: 60000.

OPENCONDITIONS_EGRESS_ALLOWED_HOSTS.title: Egress allowed private hosts
OPENCONDITIONS_EGRESS_ALLOWED_HOSTS.description: Comma-separated hostnames the egress guard lets the service fetch although they resolve to private addresses, e.g. overpass for a self-hosted Overpass on the compose network. Empty: none.

OPENCONDITIONS_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES.title: Artifact download cap (bytes)
OPENCONDITIONS_DOWNLOAD_MAX_BYTES.description: Largest artifact (PBF extract) a download streams. Empty: 8 GiB.

OPENCONDITIONS_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS.title: Artifact download timeout (ms)
OPENCONDITIONS_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT_MS.description: Overall timeout of an artifact download. Empty: 30 minutes.

RATE_LIMIT_MAX.title: Rate limit: requests per window
RATE_LIMIT_MAX.description: Requests one client may make per rate-limit window.

STREAM_MAX_CONNECTIONS.title: Live streams open at once
STREAM_MAX_CONNECTIONS.description: Server-sent-event streams the service holds open at once.

TRUST_PROXY_CIDRS.title: Trusted proxy ranges
TRUST_PROXY_CIDRS.description: Immediate reverse-proxy address ranges to trust for client IPs; only one proxy hop is accepted.

OPENCONDITIONS_RAW_MAX_BYTES.title: Raw archive cap (bytes)
OPENCONDITIONS_RAW_MAX_BYTES.description: Cap on the raw payload archive's stored bytes; 0 = no cap. Empty: 10 GiB.

OPENCONDITIONS_HISTORY_DAYS.title: Record history (days)
OPENCONDITIONS_HISTORY_DAYS.description: How long a tombstoned record and its revisions stay for the history API. Empty: 90.

OPENCONDITIONS_ON_DEMAND_DEADLINE_MS.title: On-demand read deadline (ms)
OPENCONDITIONS_ON_DEMAND_DEADLINE_MS.description: How long a read waits for its on-demand fetches before it answers from storage. Empty: 3000.

OPENCONDITIONS_FEEDS_REMOTE_URL.title: Remote feed bundle URL
OPENCONDITIONS_FEEDS_REMOTE_URL.description: URL of a remote feed bundle ({ "files": { "<domain>/<region>": <region file>, "credentials": <credentials file> } }, e.g. a published atlas/<domain>.json) to pull feeds from: the way to run a custom catalogue here, whose feeds add to or override the baked-in feeds by id. Only used when remote-pull is enabled.

OPENCONDITIONS_FEEDS_REMOTE_ENABLED.title: Enable remote feed-pull
OPENCONDITIONS_FEEDS_REMOTE_ENABLED.description: Set to "true" to opt the instance into remote-pull (default off). The bundle is checked like the baked catalogue and every URL is egress-guarded; a snapshot is kept on the service's volume so the instance survives the remote being down.

OPENCONDITIONS_INSTANCE_ID.title: Instance id
OPENCONDITIONS_INSTANCE_ID.description: This instance's stable id, the namespace of every record it originates and its name to federation peers: lower-case letters, digits, dots and dashes, e.g. maps.example.org. Set it before federating, and to the same value as the contributions API's. Empty: local.

OPENCONDITIONS_ARCHIVE_KEEP_NIGHTS.title: Archive nights kept
OPENCONDITIONS_ARCHIVE_KEEP_NIGHTS.description: Nights of dated files the nightly archive keeps; 0 keeps every night. Empty: 30.

ARCHIVE_CRON.title: Archive schedule
ARCHIVE_CRON.description: Cron of the nightly archive build (UTC); "off" disables it. Empty: 30 3 * * *.

SEGMENT_PROFILE_CRON.title: Segment profile schedule
SEGMENT_PROFILE_CRON.description: Cron of the weekly segment speed-profile derivation (UTC); "off" disables it. Empty: 30 3 * * 1.

SEGMENT_REBUILD_CRON.title: Segment rebuild schedule
SEGMENT_REBUILD_CRON.description: Cron of the weekly road-graph segment rebuild (UTC); "off" disables it. Empty: 0 4 * * 1.

OPENCONDITIONS_SHRINK_TRIPWIRE_RATIO.title: Shrink tripwire ratio
OPENCONDITIONS_SHRINK_TRIPWIRE_RATIO.description: An event feed's complete snapshot whose count does not exceed this share of its last published count is skipped as a likely partial parse, e.g. 0.1. Empty or 0: only a drop to zero is skipped.

OPENCONDITIONS_MAX_FEED_BYTES.title: Feed response cap (bytes)
OPENCONDITIONS_MAX_FEED_BYTES.description: Largest feed response, compressed or decompressed. Empty: 256 MiB.

OPENCONDITIONS_MAX_REDIRECTS.title: Feed redirects
OPENCONDITIONS_MAX_REDIRECTS.description: Redirects a feed fetch follows. Empty: 5.

OPENCONDITIONS_MAX_OBSERVATIONS_PER_POLL.title: Readings per poll
OPENCONDITIONS_MAX_OBSERVATIONS_PER_POLL.description: Cap on the readings one poll may hold; a poll above it fails. Empty: 1000000.

OPENCONDITIONS_OSM_MAXSPEED_FALLBACK.title: OSM maxspeed fallback
OPENCONDITIONS_OSM_MAXSPEED_FALLBACK.description: "false" turns off the nightly fallback that fills a sensor without a speed baseline from OpenStreetMap maxspeed tags. Empty: on.

OPENCONDITIONS_RAW_ZSTD_LEVEL.title: Raw archive compression level
OPENCONDITIONS_RAW_ZSTD_LEVEL.description: zstd level of the raw payload archive. Empty: 9.

OPENCONDITIONS_RAW_HOT_HOURS.title: Raw archive: hours kept whole
OPENCONDITIONS_RAW_HOT_HOURS.description: Hours every distinct raw payload is kept. Empty: 48.

OPENCONDITIONS_RAW_THIN_DAYS_SITUATION.title: Raw archive: days thinned (situation feeds)
OPENCONDITIONS_RAW_THIN_DAYS_SITUATION.description: Days situation feeds then keep one raw payload an hour. Empty: 14.

OPENCONDITIONS_RAW_THIN_DAYS_OBSERVATION.title: Raw archive: days thinned (flow feeds)
OPENCONDITIONS_RAW_THIN_DAYS_OBSERVATION.description: Days flow feeds then keep one raw payload an hour. Empty: 7.

OPENCONDITIONS_ROLLUP_HOURLY_DAYS.title: Hourly rollups kept (days)
OPENCONDITIONS_ROLLUP_HOURLY_DAYS.description: Days hourly reading rollups are kept. Empty: 35.

OPENCONDITIONS_ROLLUP_DAILY_DAYS.title: Daily rollups kept (days)
OPENCONDITIONS_ROLLUP_DAILY_DAYS.description: Days daily reading rollups are kept. Empty: 400.

AU_NSW_TFNSW_API_KEY.title: Transport for NSW Open Data API key (Australia)
AU_NSW_TFNSW_API_KEY.description: An Open Data Hub API token, sent as the 'apikey' authorization header. Serves the Live Traffic hazards, the Park&Ride car parks and the Live Traffic cameras.

steps: Register for a free account at opendata.transport.nsw.gov.au and log in to the Open Data Hub.
Click your profile icon, choose 'API Tokens', enter a name, click 'CREATE API TOKEN' and copy the key (shown only once).
In the data catalogue, open the 'Car park API' and 'Live Traffic Cameras API' datasets and subscribe each to your application; the token alone authorises the live-hazard endpoints.
Paste the generated token here (sent as the 'apikey' authorization header).
x-openmapx-setup.notes: CC-BY-4.0; attribution "Transport for NSW". One token for the hazards, car-park and camera feeds.

AU_QLD_TRAFFIC_EVENTS_API_KEY.title: QLDTraffic API key (Australia) — optional
AU_QLD_TRAFFIC_EVENTS_API_KEY.description: Optional. A public key is bundled by default; set this only to use your own quota.

x-openmapx-setup.notes: Optional — the bundled public key is shared + rate-limited (100 req/min). Set your own to avoid 429s.

email.subject: QLDTraffic API key request

AU_VIC_TRANSPORTVIC_API_KEY.title: Transport Victoria Open Data key
AU_VIC_TRANSPORTVIC_API_KEY.description: Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key header value from the Transport Victoria Open Data Portal. Serves the Freeway Travel Time feed and the planned and unplanned disruption feeds.

steps: Create an account at opendata.transport.vic.gov.au (email verification + authenticator 2FA).
Open My Account → Profile → API tokens; the key is generated there.
Copy the key and set it as the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key value.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: CC-BY-4.0 (Freeway Travel Time — NOT the CC-BY-NC Bluetooth feed); attribution "Department of Transport and Planning (Victoria)". Rate limit 5 req/min.

CA_ON_511_API_KEY.title: Ontario 511 developer key (Canada)
CA_ON_511_API_KEY.description: Sent as the 'key' query parameter. Serves the Ontario 511 events, construction projects, road conditions and cameras feeds.

steps: Create a free account at 511on.ca/my511/register (or log in); an account is needed before a key can be requested.

Request a Developer API key from the developer resources page. The request names your organisation and primary contact, describes the proposed service, and identifies every third party that will receive, redistribute or display Ontario 511 data through it (for an OpenMapX instance: OpenMapX, and federation peers if federation is on).
The Ministry reviews requests case by case; once granted, copy the key (sent as the 'key' query parameter).
x-openmapx-setup.notes: Developer's Access Agreement: https://511on.ca/developers/resources. Data under the Open Government Licence – Ontario; the disclaimer travels with the data when it is distributed. Ontario 511 allows ten calls every 60 seconds per key. Each of the four feeds paces itself to that limit on its own, not together; their cadences (five minutes for the events, construction projects and road conditions, an hour for the cameras) keep the four well inside ten calls a minute.

MOBILITHEK_CERT.title: Mobilithek — client certificate (PEM)
MOBILITHEK_CERT.description: PEM contents of the machine-account client certificate (mutual TLS). ONE certificate authenticates every Mobilithek feed — set it once, then just add each feed's subscription id. Recommended: generate your own keypair with `openssl req -x509 -newkey rsa:4096 -nodes -days 825 -keyout mobilithek.key.pem -out mobilithek.cert.pem -subj "/CN=openmapx-mobilithek"`, upload mobilithek.cert.pem under the machine account's 'Zertifikat hochladen' tab (no SMS needed), then paste mobilithek.cert.pem here and mobilithek.key.pem in the key field. Alternative: convert an issued .p12 with `openssl pkcs12 -in m.p12 -clcerts -nokeys | openssl x509` (cert) and `openssl pkcs12 -in m.p12 -nocerts -nodes | openssl rsa` (key).

steps: Register your organisation at mobilithek.info/registration-request; leave 'Organisation relevant gemäß MDV/PBefG' unchecked.
Subscribe to the offer(s) you want (each feed's offer IDs are listed in its subscription-id field).

Create a machine account at mobilithek.info/organisation/machine-accounts and upload your own certificate (generate it with the openssl command shown in this field's description, no SMS needed). Paste the certificate PEM here and its private key in the key field.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: This ONE certificate authenticates every Mobilithek feed — set it once, then add each feed's subscription id. (The NRW state network is published under 'LVZ.NRW', not 'Straßen.NRW'.)

MOBILITHEK_KEY.title: Mobilithek — client private key (PEM)
MOBILITHEK_KEY.description: PEM contents of the certificate's private key, with no passphrase (generate with openssl -nodes, or strip an issued .p12 key with openssl rsa). Stays with us — never uploaded to Mobilithek. Shared by every Mobilithek feed.

steps: Register on the data exchanger (Dataudveksleren) using an eID — choose 'International' for an eID from another European country. Leave the 'Dataowner consent' checkbox unchecked (it's the publisher agreement).
Create a service account at du-portal-ui.dataudveksler.app.vd.dk/profile/service-accounts.

Associate the service account with dataset 416 (Traffic Events and Road Works snapshot — NOT 415, which is AMQP-only). The dataset page then shows the data-access URL and the credential the service account presents.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: CC-BY-4.0; attribution "Vejdirektoratet." Access is via a service account, not a plain API key — confirm from the dataset page whether its credential is a header/query token or an OAuth2 client-credentials pair.

steps: Register for the DATEX II API at tarktee.transpordiamet.ee/#/en/datex-registration (Transpordiamet 'Smart Road' gateway); a key is issued after registration. The old tarktee.mnt.ee domain is retired.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: CC-BY-4.0 (commercial OK).

steps: Register / sign in at developer.data.nationalhighways.co.uk/signin.

Subscribe to the 'unlimited' product at developer.data.nationalhighways.co.uk/subscription#product=unlimited (one product grants the APIM key for all NTIS DATEX feeds, incl. Road and Lane Closures v2.0).
Copy the Ocp-Apim-Subscription-Key from your profile at developer.data.nationalhighways.co.uk/profile.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: OGL-UK-3.0; attribution "Contains National Highways data © Crown copyright and database right."

HR_HC_USER.title: Hrvatske ceste (Croatia) — B2B username
HR_HC_USER.description: HTTP Basic username for the promet-info B2B feeds (Croatia).

steps: There is no self-service portal — request B2B account credentials from Hrvatske ceste (the promet-info operator), via hrvatske-ceste.hr or the data.gov.hr dataset page.
Ask for the events publication ("HC Prometni događaji DatexII v3") to be enabled on the account as well as roadworks — the two are authorised separately.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: Open licence (commercial OK); access is gated on the B2B account.

steps: Request a free account for the DATEX II server via the 'Get access' page (Open data → What is DATEX → Get access).
x-openmapx-setup.notes: NLOD-2.0 (commercial OK). One account serves the events and the traffic-speed feeds.

SE_TRAFIKVERKET_API_KEY.title: Trafikverket key (Sweden)
SE_TRAFIKVERKET_API_KEY.description: Authentication key: sent as ?authenticationkey= to the DATEX II situation feed and in the POST request body to the traffic-flow feed.

steps: Sign up at data.trafikverket.se/oauth2/Account/register.
Create an authentication key under data.trafikverket.se/mypage/systems (My systems).
x-openmapx-setup.notes: CC0 — no restrictions. API endpoint: api.trafikinfo.trafikverket.se/v2/data.json (the bare host has no web page).

steps: Request an API account via the form at datamall.lta.gov.sg/content/datamall/en/request-for-api.html.
The AccountKey is emailed to you.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: Singapore ODL (commercial OK); attribution to the Land Transport Authority. Serves the Traffic Incidents and Traffic Speed Bands feeds.

steps: Register at nap.si/en/registration (DARS / DRSI).

Request access and tick exactly the two DATEX II v3.3 datasets (under 'Other contents', XML, english): 'Traffic events (DATEX II v3.3)' and 'Roadworks (DATEX II v3.3)'. Leave everything else unticked.

Fill the Purpose/Description (min. 100 chars), set a Time period, agree to the terms, and submit. Ready-to-paste purpose: OpenMapX (https://openmapx.com) is a free, open-source maps and navigation app; we ingest the Traffic events and Roadworks DATEX II v3.3 datasets to display live road conditions and route around closures and roadworks in Slovenia, with CC-BY-SA attribution shown to users.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: CC-BY-SA (ShareAlike). The B2B host (b2b.ncup.si) is credential-gated; the NAP account is sent as HTTP Basic — confirm the exact scheme when granted.

steps: Register for a free OHGO developer account at ohgo.com/developer and create an API key.
Set US_OH_OHGO_API_KEY to the key value; the feeds activate on the next scheduler cycle.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: Free key. Data is U.S. government public domain. Serves the travel delays, construction and incidents feeds.

DE_TANKERKOENIG_FUEL_API_KEY.title: Tankerkönig API Key
DE_TANKERKOENIG_FUEL_API_KEY.description: Tankerkoenig API key for German fuel prices.

steps: Open onboarding.tankerkoenig.de (linked from creativecommons.tankerkoenig.de via 'API-Key').
Enter a working email address and describe your non-commercial use case.
Agree to the CC BY 4.0 terms (attribution to tankerkoenig.de required).
Submit the form; registration is reviewed manually and can take a few days.
Receive the API key by email once approved.
x-openmapx-setup.cost: Free for non-commercial use (commercial use needs a paid agreement).
x-openmapx-setup.notes: Data is CC BY 4.0 (MTS-K) — attribution required. Free-tier limits: 1 request/min, 25 km radius.

email.subject: Tankerkönig API key request (non-commercial)
email.body:
Hello,

I would like to request a free non-commercial Tankerkönig API key.

Use case: displaying current German fuel prices in a self-hosted, non-commercial OpenMapX map application.

I agree to the CC BY 4.0 terms and will attribute the data to tankerkoenig.de.

Thank you.

OVERPASS_URL.title: Overpass URL
OVERPASS_URL.description: Base URL of the Overpass instance (http://overpass:80, https://overpass-api.de) or its full interpreter URL (http://overpass:80/api/interpreter), as OpenMapX's OVERPASS_URL accepts: queries go to the base URL plus /api/interpreter. Defaults to the public instance, which allows about 10,000 requests a day; point it at a self-hosted Overpass for heavier use. A private host also needs OPENCONDITIONS_EGRESS_ALLOWED_HOSTS.

DE_DB_BAHNPARK_PARKING_CLIENT_ID.title: DB BahnPark client ID
DE_DB_BAHNPARK_PARKING_CLIENT_ID.description: The client ID of a DB API Marketplace application subscribed to Parking Information (DB BahnPark).

steps: Register/log in to the DB API Marketplace via 'DB Kundenkonto'.
Create an application with 'Neue Anwendung erstellen'.
In the Katalog, open 'Parking Information Service - DB BahnPark' and subscribe the free Testzugang plan.
Open the application's details and copy its Client ID into this field.
x-openmapx-setup.cost: Free: Testzugang allows up to 1,000 transactions/month (max 10 req/min), no approval.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: Provides ~315 DB BahnPark facilities. The higher transit-authority plan needs a separate data agreement.

DE_DB_BAHNPARK_PARKING_API_KEY.title: DB BahnPark API key
DE_DB_BAHNPARK_PARKING_API_KEY.description: The client secret of the same DB API Marketplace application.

steps: Register/log in to the DB API Marketplace and create an application ('Neue Anwendung erstellen').
Copy the Client Secret (API key) shown once during application creation.
Subscribe ('Abonnieren') the 'Parking Information Service - DB BahnPark' Testzugang plan to that application.
Paste the Client Secret here (sent as the DB-Api-Key header).
x-openmapx-setup.cost: Free: Testzugang allows up to 1,000 transactions/month (max 10 req/min), no approval.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: The Client Secret is displayed only once at creation; regenerate it in the application settings if lost.

GB_ENG_NETRAVELDATA_PARKING_USERNAME.title: NE Travel Data username
GB_ENG_NETRAVELDATA_PARKING_USERNAME.description: The username of a netraveldata.co.uk account; the website login is the API credential.

steps: Go to the UTMC Open Data Service (NE Travel Data) at netraveldata.co.uk and register a free account via the 'Register' link.
Confirm your registration email and set a password.
Use the username you signed up with as this value — the same site account credentials authenticate the API feeds.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: This is the Newcastle / Tyne & Wear (UTMC) feed at netraveldata.co.uk — not a Glasgow contact. The website login you create is the API credential.

email.subject: API access request — UTMC Open Data Service (car park feed)
email.body:
Hello,

I would like to access the UTMC / NE Travel Data open-data API, in particular the car park occupancy feeds for Tyne & Wear / Newcastle.

I have registered an account on netraveldata.co.uk; could you please confirm that my account credentials are enabled for API access, or advise if any additional registration step is required?

Intended use: integrating live car-park availability into an open-source mapping application.

Thank you,
[Your name]

GB_ENG_NETRAVELDATA_PARKING_PASSWORD.title: NE Travel Data password
GB_ENG_NETRAVELDATA_PARKING_PASSWORD.description: The password of the same netraveldata.co.uk account.

steps: During registration on netraveldata.co.uk, set (or reset) the password for your account.
Use that account password as this value.
The username + password pair is sent as HTTP credentials when fetching the UTMC car-park feed.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: Same netraveldata.co.uk account as the UTMC username — there is no separate API password; the website login doubles as the API credential.

OCM_CHARGING_API_KEY.title: Open Charge Map API key
OCM_CHARGING_API_KEY.description: An Open Charge Map application key.

x-openmapx-setup.urlLabel: Get Open Charge Map API key
steps: Go to openchargemap.org and create an account or sign in.
Open 'My Profile' → 'My Apps'.
Click 'Register an Application' and enter a name and description.
Copy the API key issued immediately.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: Required for regular use and for calls with maxresults > 250. Sent via the 'X-API-Key' header or 'key' query parameter.

NO_NOBIL_CHARGING_API_KEY.title: NOBIL API key
NO_NOBIL_CHARGING_API_KEY.description: A NOBIL API v3 key, issued by email per registered website.

steps: Open info.nobil.no/api and review the Creative Commons (CC BY 4.0) terms.
Use the 'Ask for an API-key' section to contact NOBIL with your project details.
Accept the CC BY 4.0 terms of use.
Receive the API key by email.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: Norway/Sweden charging data. The request is handled by email rather than an instant self-service form.

email.subject: NOBIL API key request
email.body:
Hello,

I would like to request a NOBIL API key (API v3) to display Norwegian/Swedish EV charging station data in a self-hosted OpenMapX map application.

I have read and accept the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0) terms of use and will attribute NOBIL accordingly.

Project: self-hosted, non-commercial mapping application.

x-openmapx-setup.urlLabel: Register for an LTA DataMall AccountKey
steps: Open datamall.lta.gov.sg and go to 'Request for API Access'.
Register with your name, email, and organisation, and accept the Singapore Open Data Licence.
Confirm your email; the AccountKey is issued to your registered email.

x-openmapx-setup.notes: Covers the EV Charging Points APIs (station location, connector types, real-time availability by postal code). Sent via the 'AccountKey' header, never as a query parameter.

SI_NAP_CHARGING_USERNAME.title: NAP Slovenija account email
SI_NAP_CHARGING_USERNAME.description: The email of the NAP business-entity account that holds access to the Prometej IDACS datasets.

steps: Create a business-entity account at nap.si (click the user icon → Registration) and confirm the email.
Log in, open your profile, and request permission for the 'Prometej IDACS Energy Infrastructure Table (DATEX II v3.6)' dataset. Accept the general terms of use.
Also request the 'Prometej IDACS Energy Infrastructure Status' dataset for live status.
Wait for NAP to grant the requests (shown as 'granted' on your profile page).
Enter the account's email here and its password in the password field; requests use HTTP Basic auth.

SI_NAP_CHARGING_PASSWORD.title: NAP Slovenija account password
SI_NAP_CHARGING_PASSWORD.description: The password of that NAP account.

x-openmapx-setup.urlLabel: Register for a TDX platform account
steps: Go to tdx.transportdata.tw/register and create a free platform member account.
Sign in, open Member Center → 資料服務 → 服務金鑰 (API Key).
Create a Client Id / Client Secret pair (up to 3 per account).
Copy both values — the Client Secret is only shown once.

The free tier's quota (about 4,500 calls a month at 5 a minute) is the account's, shared by both feeds.

TW_TDX_CLIENT_SECRET.description: The secret of the same Client Id / Client Secret pair.

US_NY_511_API_KEY.title: 511NY data feed access (New York)
US_NY_511_API_KEY.description: The access NYSDOT grants under the 511NY Developer Access Agreement, for the events and winter road conditions feeds (and the camera inventory).

x-openmapx-setup.urlLabel: Read the 511NY data feed page and Developer Access Agreement
steps: Read the Developer Access Agreement on 511ny.org/help/24 (last updated 2026-09-18). Submitting a request accepts it.

Open the request form linked on that page ("CARS Agencies' XML Feed Request Form", shared by several state DOTs). Fill in Name, "Company, Agency, or Personal Use", the company or project name, and the email the approval should go to, and tick NY under the agencies.

Reason for Access is the only free-text field, so it must cover what the agreement asks a request to describe: the intended use and the product (name the traffic events, winter road conditions and camera inventory feeds); the intended market and the benefit to travelers; any similar products you have built or plan; and every intermediate or third-party disseminator. Name OpenConditions, the self-hosted data service that fetches the feeds for your map, and, if this instance serves its public API or federates with peers, those as recipients too. Then state that you accept the agreement and its attribution and display duties.

Ready-to-adapt reason: "I am requesting access to the NYSDOT (511NY) XML data feeds (traffic events, winter road conditions and the camera inventory) for OpenMapX, a free, non-commercial, open-source maps and navigation app. Our instance fetches the feeds through OpenConditions, our own self-hosted traffic data service, and shows live incidents, road work, closures, winter road conditions and traffic cameras on the map and in route planning, so travelers in New York can plan around them. Audience: the general public, free of charge. Similar products: none. Recipients: our app's end users through OpenConditions, operated by us; no other third parties, and we will tell NYSDOT before that changes. We will show when each report was published or last updated, keep the meaning of every report as NYSDOT published it, pass on NYSDOT's disclaimer, and credit 511NY / NYSDOT as the source. We accept the 511NY Developer Access Agreement."

Requests are reviewed weekly. An approval email brings the feed addresses, the access credential and the documentation. Send those to whoever maintains this OpenConditions instance: the feeds need their new addresses, and a reader if the format differs from the retired IBI 511 API, before they can be enabled.
x-openmapx-setup.notes: Agreement duties: show when each report was published or last updated; keep the meaning of every report as published; use best efforts to pass on NYSDOT's disclaimer; keep NYSDOT informed of changes to your product, distribution plans and recipients. Permitted, not required: the "powered by 511NY" tag line with the unaltered 511NY logo and a link to 511ny.org; otherwise "511NY" may not be used to market or brand your product. Questions and feed problems go to the 511NY program manager named on 511ny.org/help/24. The old 511ny.org developer keys and API no longer work.
